newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares end lower but set to rise on US data.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares end lower but set to rise on US data.

text.p: Danish share prices closed slightly lower on Tuesday but dealers saw them following the bond market up on Wednesday in the wake of the afternoon's positive U.S. employment cost and durable goods data.

"The latest American data was stronger than expected and helped bonds up and shares to rally although the index closed down a little. Tomorrow we should see solid gains with shares up one percent," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.17 point down at 156.09 in overall bourse turnover of 776 million crowns.
The KFX June future rose 0.15 point to 155.25 with 61 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Leading banks rose a little, while Moeller's D/S 1912 and D/S Svendborg put on 3,000 and 1,100 crowns respectively to close at 210,000 and 300,100.
Radiometer was in focus, shedding 30 crowns to end at 350 on competition fears.
